subject: Nova pilot: model shortlist, benchmarks, and next steps
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara@novacorp.com>

Cc: jake.turner@novacorp.com

Subject: Re: Nova pilot follow-up / demo recap

Hi Diego —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and a handful of clarifying questions before we lock the pilot scope.

Use case: triage + summarization of incoming customer support tickets (English, Spanish). Goal is to pre-classify priority and generate 1–2 sentence customer-visible summary.

Non-functional priorities:
- Latency: 90th percentile <= 300ms for the short summaries in steady state.
- Cost: mid-sensitivity — we need predictable per-ticket economics as volume grows (50k–200k tickets/month).
- Quality: high precision on priority classification; summaries should avoid hallucinations (especially SLA & timeframe claims).
- Compliance: PII redaction pre-processing required.

You mentioned a 2-week pilot with Redwood Dedicated capacity to validate latency and a small eval dataset. Jake (cc) will coordinate procurement and budget.

As a next step, could you send a recommended shortlist with cost/latency/quality tradeoffs, a sample prompt set we can run against our 1k eval set, and any benchmark links? Also flag any regression risks we should watch for.

Attachments: I’ve uploaded a short sample of anonymized tickets to the Drive link you provided during the call.

Thanks — looking forward to recommendations.

—Sara
Sara Lim
Product Manager, NovaCorp
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara@novacorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 18:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nova pilot follow-up / demo recap

Sara — thanks for the clear recap and the sample dataset. Below is a concise recommended shortlist and the rationale focused on the tradeoffs you highlighted (latency, cost, quality). I also included immediate next steps for the 2-week pilot.

Shortlist (recommended order)
1) redwood-rt-medium-v2 (quantized)
   - Rationale: Best balance of tail latency and cost for short-summary use cases. Optimized for continuous batching and KV caching in our serving runtime.
   - Expected latency: 60–180ms p50–p95 on Dedicated T4-equivalent pools (single-request mode with small batching).
   - Cost: ~ $0.60 per 1k tokens (quantized path), low inference cost relative to larger families.
   - Quality: Strong on classification and concise summaries; lower risk of factual hallucination for short outputs when paired with a constrained prompt.
   - Regression risk: Low-medium. Watch for changes in tokenizer behavior on edge-case punctuation.

2) meta-llama-65b-q4 (open quantized 65B)
   - Rationale: Higher-quality, better at preserving context and nuanced classification, but materially higher cost/latency.
   - Expected latency: 240–420ms p95 on Dedicated A10-equivalent pools (with optimized kernels).
   - Cost: ~ $3.20 per 1k tokens (quantized 4-bit path).
   - Quality: Highest out-of-the-box classification fidelity for subtle priority signals (tone, implied urgency).
   - Regression risk: Medium-high if you change prompt scaffolding or input distribution (long ticket histories).

3) openbench-13b-8bit
   - Rationale: Good low-cost baseline for initial A/B tests, faster than 65B but lower classification nuance.
   - Expected latency: 40–150ms p95 on T4-equivalent pools.
   - Cost: ~ $0.35 per 1k tokens.
   - Quality: Adequate for straightforward tickets; struggles with ambiguous/complex cases.
   - Regression risk: Low; simpler architecture means more stable behavior across prompt tweaks.

Operational recommendations
- Pilot plan: Start with redwood-rt-medium-v2 as the default route, route ambiguous cases to meta-llama-65b-q4 via canary/fallback for human review.
- Eval plan: Run your 1k eval set against the three models with our sample prompt_set (attached) and return per-ticket precision/recall and hallucination flags.
- Guardrails: Add a strict template for summary outputs (length-limited, no dates/commitments unless explicitly present). Use prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts.
- Regression monitoring: We’ll supply a small regression harness (prompt + golden summaries) and setup automated quality alerts tied to weekly evals.

Attachments (for your review)
- nova_benchmarks_q4.csv (sample latency and cost runs on our staging pools)
- prompt_set_v1.txt (starter prompt set used in the demo)

Links
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bNovaPilotEval
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/central/7482

Next steps
- I’ll schedule the pilot kickoff for the week of Nov 9 if that works.
- Marissa will share a slightly expanded prompt pack and the regression criteria for your eval team.
- Procurement: Jake to confirm purchase order / Dedicated reservation.

If helpful, we can also provide a short script to measure tokenized length distribution of your tickets (helps confirm cost projections).

Best —

Sara / team — adding a few concrete artifacts to run the eval quickly. Diego’s shortlist maps to the recommended pilot lanes; below are practical notes on how we ran the benchmarks and what to look for in results.

Attached: prompt_set_v2.txt (expanded prompts), regression_criteria.md (how we flag quality regressions).

Quick notes on benchmarking methodology
- For latency: we ran 1k requests against each engine with 95% realistic ticket length distribution (we’ll share the exact seed). Use production-like networking to match p95.
- For cost estimates: we measured end-to-end tokens for the full prompt + model output. Quantized engines reduce compute but watch encoding/tokenization variance.
- For quality: we compare model summaries against the golden labels with a small set of heuristic checks (hallucination heuristics: presence of dates, commitments, fabricated numbers).

Prompt engineering guidance (high level)
- Constrain output: "Return a one-sentence summary (max 18 words). If ticket contains a date or SLA promise, return 'see ticket' instead of inventing dates."
- Use a classification prefix to get high precision: explicit labels with examples (few-shot) for priority mapping (P0/P1/P2).
- For Spanish tickets: include explicit language detection + language-specific prompt templates.

Fallback policy (practical)
- Route requests to meta-llama-65b-q4 when: confidence < 0.65 OR ticket length > 1024 tokens OR user flag indicates ambiguous content.
- For high-volume low-cost operations, keep openbench-13b-8bit as the recovery lane to absorb spikes.

Deliverables we’ll push to the Drive (and attach to HubSpot)
- prompt_set_v2.txt
- regression_criteria.md
- quick-start script: pilot_tokenizer_check.sh

I’ll be available next week for a 30-minute kickoff to step through the eval harness. Diego / Ben — if you have additional perf runs (p50/p95 in different batch sizes), please drop them in the Drive folder.

Cheers —
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
